author: 阿星
content:
﻿# 挣扎4年不赚钱，现在月入$3.5万

## 冷启动：大学辍学，只为自由

六年前，Jack 从大学 last semester 辍学。

To make money online。

他不想 work traditional job。

Want to be in control of daily schedule and work。

Realized he would be miserable employee。

所以，他 tried everything：

- Print-on-demand T-shirt designs
- Affiliate marketing blog posts
- YouTube videos — 2000+ videos in under two years
- Crypto — made money and lost it all

Finally，三年前，decided to learn to code and build own apps。

## 反直觉：哭着做产品，结果成了

Most of his focus currently goes into Post Bridge。

Social media scheduling tool for small teams。

Featuring agent-friendly workflows。

Launched it one and a half years ago。

Generates $50K CAD ($35K USD) MRR。

Last six months，doubled MRR after eight-month plateau。

但最动人的故事是什么？

三个月前 Post Bridge's creation。

他在 walk with now-fiancée。

Broke down crying。

Thought he was failure。

Been trying to make money online for four years。

Spent year learning to code。

Still struggling to break $3K/mo。

But then，he lucked out。

In attempt to grow first mobile app。

Posting multiple TikToks daily。

Then cross-posting to four other platforms — all manually。

Didn't scale。

So made API-based scheduling solution。

Shared it on Twitter。

Despite lack of followers，it blew up。

Many others wanted it too！

## 暴击：一个人，一个月，$3.5万

Knowing people eagerly awaited its release was huge motivation。

Helped him work long days for month。

And it didn't feel like work。

Quite fun and exciting，even when everything was breaking。

Built Post Bridge from scratch in about month。

Only worked on few initial platforms。

Fraction of what he supports now。

Cost nothing except time to build。

Now that he has users，costs between $100 and $200 per month。

He did it all alone，and still does。

Only exception is some contractors hired while back to clean few things up。

Tech stack includes Next.js and simple backend hosted separately for API with Unkey + Supabase。

Now uses R2 for storage because Supabase egress costs were about $1,000 month and growing。

(R2 is zero，which is nice)。

Early on，faced significant challenges：

Frequently attacked and DDoS'd because Post Bridge was public。

Additionally，some people took issue with his success as new coder。

Since then，learned lot。

Adding rate limits、enhanced security、monitors for these issues，plus Vercel WAF。

##  punchline：没有免费套餐，只有硬墙

He first makes every app for himself，then prices it and releases it。

Learned not to offer free plans。

Instead，relies on hard paywalls or credit card-based free trials to generate revenue。

One exception is mobile app that generated significant revenue，which is freemium (Lovelee Couples App)。

Charge for your product。

Don't fear low sales。

This filters out noise and forces you to provide real value。

Which is essential for success！

It's very good thing！

For growth，he posts thoughts on X。

Makes videos on TikTok and Instagram。

Also created dev logs on YouTube for year。

Posts new features，but those quickly become stale and bloated。

So often finds new ways to articulate core concepts or showcase existing features。

For example，created TikTok format and reused it 300 times。

Modifying parts until views declined。

Brought over 30,000 downloads to one of mobile apps。

This all helped explain what he does and its interest and value to others。

People connect better with other people than with AI-generated content or ads。

Allowed him to build Twitter following related to SaaS niche。

Though following grew mostly after success，not before。

**他的 advice：**

Follow your curiosity and interests instead of what is trending or best business market to enter。

If you don't enjoy your work，your chances of success are slim。

People who enjoy their work don't feel like they're working。

Which helps them persist and go further。

Even with limited resources。

Beyond that，take it one day at time and be grateful you are alive。

And KEEP GOING！
